title: Real-Time Lakehouse Streaming ETL Pipeline with Apache Spark, Delta Lake, Kafka & MinIO
problem: Traditional corporate data platforms relying on overnight batch ETL jobs inflict a 24-hour analytical lag on decision makers, preventing fraud detection, inventory rebalancing, and live operational monitoring. Naive streaming architectures built on raw object storage suffer from dirty reads, duplicate event writes, corrupt file fragmentation (the small-file problem), and lack of ACID transactional guarantees when streaming jobs fail mid-microbatch. This project builds a production-grade real-time lakehouse streaming ETL pipeline in Python using Apache Spark Structured Streaming, Delta Lake, and Apache Kafka. The pipeline ingests high-velocity events into a Medallion architecture (Bronze raw, Silver cleaned/deduplicated, Gold aggregated business marts), enforces ACID transactions with Delta Lake write-ahead logs, executes stateful stream-stream joins with event-time watermarking, and stores Parquet datasets in MinIO (S3-compatible) object storage with sub-5s end-to-end latency.

use_cases.title: FinTech Fraud Detection & Live Transaction Scoring
use_cases.first_sentence: Credit card networks processing thousands of point-of-sale swipes per second must detect fraudulent spending bursts across merchant categories.
use_cases.second_sentence: The streaming pipeline consumes transaction events from Kafka, dedupes events using watermarks in Spark, and updates rolling user spending profiles in Delta Lake tables within 4 seconds.

use_cases.title: Ride-Hailing Dynamic Surge Pricing & Supply Balancing
use_cases.first_sentence: Urban ride-hailing platforms need to match passenger ride requests with available driver locations in localized geographic zones.
use_cases.second_sentence: The Spark engine executes stateful stream-stream joins between passenger requests and driver GPS pings, computing localized supply-demand ratios in real time.

use_cases.title: E-Commerce Real-Time Inventory Ledger Reconciliation
use_cases.first_sentence: Retail fulfillment systems distributing orders across multiple regional warehouses need an immutable audit ledger of stock decrements.
use_cases.second_sentence: The system writes ACID micro-batches to Delta Lake, guaranteeing exactly-once semantics and supporting historical time-travel audit queries for financial compliance.

hard_parts: Configuring Apache Spark Structured Streaming watermarks and event-time stateful operations to handle late-arriving events without unbounded memory leaks
Enforcing Delta Lake ACID transaction guarantees with optimistic concurrency control and idempotent checkpointing during simulated node crashes
Implementing automatic small-file compaction (OPTIMIZE / bin-packing) on streaming Delta tables to prevent query degradation over millions of Parquet files
Structuring the Medallion architecture (Bronze raw ingestion, Silver deduplicated data cleaning, Gold continuous aggregate rollups) with Delta schema evolution
screener_signals: Clean Python codebase cleanly separating Kafka ingestion schemas, Spark Structured Streaming jobs, Delta Lake table definitions, and MinIO storage configs
Streaming benchmark proving sustained ingestion of 15,000+ events per second with sub-5s end-to-end processing latency from Kafka to Delta Gold
Anti-fake verification script injecting 10 duplicate events with identical transaction IDs and 5 late-arriving events, asserting exactly-once deduplication in the Silver table

architecture.data_flow: Producers publish transaction events to Kafka; Spark Structured Streaming consumes events and writes raw payloads to the Bronze Delta table in MinIO; a secondary streaming query reads Bronze, applies a 10-minute watermark on event_time, deduplicates transactions by transaction_id, validates schemas, and appends to the Silver Delta table; a third streaming query computes 5-minute sliding window aggregations (total volume, merchant counts), writing to the Gold Delta table; downstream analytical BI dashboards query Gold Delta tables using Spark SQL; if a worker fails, Spark resumes from the S3 checkpoint with zero duplicate records.
architecture.enforcement_mechanism: Delta Lake ACID write-ahead transaction logs (`_delta_log/`) and Spark Structured Streaming WAL checkpoints ensuring exactly-once delivery.

environment.gpu: None required (purely CPU, memory, and disk I/O bound data pipeline software)
environment.cost: $0 (fully open-source stack using local Docker Desktop for Kafka, Spark, and MinIO)
environment.accounts_keys_quotas: No external AWS cloud accounts, Databricks licenses, or paid S3 quotas required
environment.reference_environment: Local 4-core CPU with Docker Desktop (Kafka, Spark standalone master, and MinIO containers) and Python 3.11

riskiest_component.name: Small File Problem and Out-of-Memory Errors in Stateful Streaming Aggregations
riskiest_component.mitigation: Configure watermarks to purge state stores after 10 minutes and schedule periodic Delta OPTIMIZE compaction jobs.
riskiest_component.fallback: Increase micro-batch trigger interval to 5 seconds to reduce generated Parquet file frequency.

worksheet.q3: 3 use cases: fintech fraud detection, ride-hailing surge pricing, and e-commerce inventory ledger reconciliation.

worksheet.q5: Hard parts: Spark watermarks and state stores, Delta Lake ACID transactions under failures, small-file Parquet compaction, and Medallion architecture.
